question: Should OpenClaw core accept bridge-backed scheduled text create/list support now, with attachments, replies, and cancel/delete deliberately unsupported?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and proven, but it exposes a new user-facing Send Later capability built on private Messages APIs, so source review cannot decide the product/API acceptance alone.

options.title: Accept Narrow Create/List Scope
options.body: After the expiring examples are fixed, merge the create/list-only scheduled text surface and keep unsupported paths fail-closed.

options.title: Hold For API Contract
options.body: Keep the PR open until maintainers define the permanent scheduled-message CLI/RPC contract and unsupported-operation semantics.

options.title: Defer Core Support
options.body: Close or pause the PR if core should not own scheduled-message behavior on private IMCore APIs yet.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Create/List Scope
recommendation.body: After the expiring examples are fixed, merge the create/list-only scheduled text surface and keep unsupported paths fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the strongest current-main and adjacent bridge-history owner for accepting the core API and private delivery-risk direction.
